pairs.evidence: app/_lib/public-base-url.ts:144 The resolver accepts one value under two names, server-only APP_BASE_URL kept 'for backward compatibility' and its NEXT_PUBLIC_ mirror, which is the dual-name alias the technique forbids. techniques.evidence: app/_lib/public-base-url.ts:144 The technique says 'a temporary alias that accepts both names is the one thing not to do'. Here a backward-compatibility alias is permanent and is reconciled only by a boot warning and publicOriginConflict.
app/_lib/public-base-url.ts:163 This builds emitted links and fetches nothing. The Host header is treated as untrusted, but there is no outbound connection to bind a check to.
app/_lib/after-response.ts:38 Deferred-task failures go only to the server log. There is no broker response to the client.

pairs.registryProposal: The alias rule is written for a value changing sides. It does not say whether a deliberate, permanent mirror of a non-secret value (a public URL, server-only name plus NEXT_PUBLIC name) counts as the forbidden alias or as an accepted dual declaration. The code here reasons it is safe because the value grants nothing, yet it still drifts. The technique could state the case outright: one name, read on both sides.
